messages:
maria (PM): Heads-up — AWS retail customer asked for a predictable 99th pct latency SLA for bursty shopping events. They want an 'opt-in' runtime dial and acceptance criteria before commit. We need to scope kernel/kv changes + rollout plan.
chen (Eng Lead): Noted. We should map ask -> technical levers: kernel selection policy, prefetching KV cache, and a conservative attention opt path.
sam (Runtime): Agreed. Quick sketch: add a routing policy that pins requests to a low-latency kernel if model seq_len <= 1024 and tokens/sec < X, otherwise fallback to high-throughput variant. Also an explicit KV prewarm for flagged sessions.
aj (Infra): Prewarm means reserved GPU memory + warmed KV store. That's capacity-heavy. We need to surface cost delta to PMs.
elaine (Solutions): Customer specifically said they can accept higher cost during promo windows. They asked for a canary plan and rollback hooks.
jon (ML): We should add eval gates — quality regressions when forcing low-latency kernel on longer contexts. Need a small prompt set of regression cases.
maria (PM): Acceptance criteria proposal (first pass): 1) 99th-pct latency <= 120ms for 95% of promo windows in canary region, 2) no >1% generation quality regression vs baseline on eval suite, 3) automated rollback on error rate >0.5%. Thoughts?
sam (Runtime): Feels reasonable. Edge cases: multi-turn chats with hidden long KV state — prewarm might be ineffective. Also kernel selection based purely on seq_len can be gamed by user prompts. We need a safe heuristic combining recent token rate + kv-size.
chen (Eng Lead): For rollout gates: dev canary -> infra canary (capacity + cost telemetry) -> small customer canary -> broader opt-in. Each stage needs explicit perf + error checks. Add SLA contract test harness.
aj (Infra): I'll add a metric in infra: `reserved_gpu_fraction` and `kv_warm_hits` plus cost-per-1000-tokens. We'll alert if cost bump > 3x baseline.
elaine (Solutions): For the customer success path, we'll expose `runtime_dial: low_latency` toggle and provide a rollout checklist and runbook for promo-day ops. Include manual kill-switch.
jon (ML): On evals: suggest 3 buckets — short Q/A, multi-turn with long history, and adversarial prompts. We'll run A/B with sampling to detect hallucination delta.
maria (PM): Request: write short PRD stub with scope (kernel policy, kv prewarm, rollout), acceptance criteria above, and a rough timeline: 4wk dev, 2wk infra canary, 2wk customer canary. Who can own the PRD?
chen (Eng Lead): I can own PRD draft with Sam and Aj. Will ping for a quick async doc by EOD tomorrow.
sam (Runtime): I'll list the kernel variants and safe heuristics. Also propose a `--force-lowlatency` debug flag for on-call.
aj (Infra): Will mock infra telemetry and estimate cost delta; need two weeks to provision canary quota.
elaine (Solutions): I'll coordinate customer readiness + acceptance evals; will collect their promo window dates.
maria (PM): Awesome — include risk section (cost, quality regression, eviction storms) and a mitigation table. Also surface rollback plan with automated rollback thresholds.
chen (Eng Lead): Noted. Quick dev question: do we want KV prewarm as synchronous blocking step or background warm? Blocking gives better guarantee but higher tail if warm fails. Thoughts?
sam (Runtime): Prefer background warm + optimistic routing: route to low-latency kernel only when `kv_warm_hits > threshold` else use baseline. That avoids blocking the request. Add instrumentation to measure `kv_miss_latency` spikes.
aj (Infra): We'll implement `kv_warm_hits` as a per-session moving avg. Need to ensure state cleanup to avoid memory leaks.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary infra stack for low-latency-dial -> 1745010300 by @aj. :rocket:
maria (PM): Great — next steps: Chen to own PRD draft, Sam/Aj to detail heuristics & telemetry, Elaine to own customer ops. Thanks team :thumbsup:
